title: Alex Hormozi's six steps to building a brand that commands 10x pricing
summary: Hormozi defines branding as pairing something unknown (you) with something people already like, then walks through six steps: what branding is, why it matters (LTV:CAC), pick the who, find what they like, advertise the pairing, and keep your promises. A strong brand lowers CAC, raises prices, and drives repeat purchase.

principles.text: Branding is just repeated pairing of what people don't know (you) with something they already know and like.
principles.quote: branding is this big fancy word but all it means is the association between two things

principles.text: Brand matters because it improves the core arbitrage: lower CAC, higher LTV, higher prices, and exclusive repeat buying.
principles.quote: if brand can allow you to convert a higher percentage of your audience get those people to buy more times from you get them to not buy from anyone else and get them to do that at a higher price

principles.text: Pick a who that is growing, can afford it, is easy to target, and is in pain.
principles.quote: these are the four basic things growing they can afford it I'm easy to find and they're in pain

principles.text: Advertising is making known; branding is what you make known. Pair yourself with what your who likes and their problems.
principles.quote: advertising is the process of making known branding is what you make known it's the content of the advertising

principles.text: What others say about you outweighs what you say, and what they experience outweighs both. Keep promises to create a virtuous cycle.
principles.quote: what other people say to them matters way more than what you tell them

principles.text: Every new association trades some audience for a better-fit one; keep one core pillar and prune what doesn't fit.
principles.quote: whenever you make an association you trade a certain percentage of your audience for ideally a greater percentage of the type of people you want
